players.product: Helios AI/HPC data-center campus (West Texas, 800 gross MW) leased to CoreWeave, plus Merlin / Caspian / Selene Texas development sites - ex-Bitcoin-mining site (Galaxy Power)

quarterly_data.signal: Christopher Ferraro: subsequent to quarter end, Galaxy completed a large load interconnect study and received approval from ERCOT for an additional 830 megawatts of power capacity at the Helios campus, which "more than doubles Helios' footprint of approved power capacity". The 830 megawatts was part of a larger request; ERCOT concluded the grid could accept an additional 830 megawatts today, and the approval came before ERCOT's new batch process is in place. The timeline to energize it depends on completion of approved transmission infrastructure, including a private substation; based on current procurement and construction schedules, Galaxy expects to begin energizing this capacity in late 2028 through early 2029 (the power "still cannot come online until late 2028. On the earliest"). With more than 1.6 gigawatts of approved power, Helios "is projected to be the largest known 100% front of the meter data center campus." Novogratz: "There is not a lot of 830 megawatt new sites of power being granted in The United States."
quarterly_data.figure: Additional 830 megawatts approved by ERCOT (more than 1.6 gigawatts approved at Helios); energization expected late 2028 through early 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Beyond the approved capacity, Galaxy has two applications totaling approximately 1.8 gigawatts of incremental requests progressing through various stages of ERCOT's load study process. Ferraro: between the prior interconnect request for the Helios campus (purchased from Argo back in 2022) and requests accumulated through land acquisitions adjacent to Helios, Galaxy has had "north of 3.5 gigawatts in total". The incremental 1.8 gigawatts will be part of ERCOT's new batch-processing framework (groups of requests studied together, with approvals parceled out pro rata step by step), so timing of the next incremental load approvals "is still a little unknown"; getting the 830 in one large chunk before the batch process was "worth its weight" for Galaxy.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 1.8 gigawatts of incremental requests in ERCOT study; north of 3.5 gigawatts of total interconnect requests

quarterly_data.signal: Phase one construction at Helios: Galaxy is prepared to deliver the first data hall to CoreWeave later in Q1 and remains on track to deliver the remaining data halls, representing the full 133 megawatts of critical IT for phase one, within the first half of the year (by the end of the second quarter). In Q4 the building was completely dried in; all generators and ehouses supporting the first data hall are set in place, every major component required to energize it is on-site and installed, and commissioning activities began in the fourth quarter. Winter storm Fern temporarily paused construction; within five days of the storm more than 1,000 subcontractors were back on-site. CFO Anthony Paquette: data-center financial results remain de minimis until Galaxy begins recognizing revenue under Phase one of the CoreWeave lease, expected to start later in Q1.
quarterly_data.figure: Full 133 megawatts of phase one critical IT on track within the first half of the year; more than 1,000 subcontractors on-site

quarterly_data.signal: Phase two at Helios: Galaxy has kicked off earth, concrete and steel work and issued purchase orders to secure critical long lead equipment for the additional building development that will house the 260 megawatts of incremental critical IT capacity for phase two. Phase two financing: Galaxy is continuing to evaluate various debt financing structures and having conversations with a select number of potential partners, focused on a disciplined capital structure that supports long-term scalability at Helios.
quarterly_data.figure: 260 megawatts of incremental critical IT capacity (phase two); long lead equipment purchase orders issued

quarterly_data.signal: Tenant search for the next 830 megawatts: Ferraro said the major tenant category is hyperscalers, a term broadening to larger neoclouds, direct model builders and "perhaps even some equipment manufacturers", all looking for large chunks of power capacity; "the ambitions have not shrunk at all", with "reiterated and elevated CapEx expectations" from a lot of companies. "all potential tenants are on the table", but availability of capital and credit on economically attractive terms is "paramount", and "already having such a large exposure to CoreWeave, means a natural focus on higher credit quality tenants" (investment-grade counterparties), with CoreWeave potentially acting as agent and GPU cluster management partner. Novogratz hopes to "have news on who's gonna occupy that site" in the next period of time. Ferraro does not expect a year-long negotiation: major players have "very quickly moved to '28, '29, '30 power", and lead times for large electrical infrastructure push delivery into early '28 at a minimum, so "you gotta pick your partner quick" and start locking up supply chain.
quarterly_data.figure: 830 megawatts available to existing or new tenants; no specific figure on lease terms

quarterly_data.signal: Lease pricing: Ferraro said pricing surprised to the upside. The initial instinct was that the dollar per kilowatt per month rental price would start high and normalize down as bigger clients came in, but "there isn't actually a very good downward trend"; given "a real choke point in available future capacity for electricity at scale", "We've actually seen base rental prices go up in a lot of cases and with Cypher as well", which plays favorably versus what Galaxy initially underwrote. Novogratz: for the next tenant Galaxy will "look at rate plus counterparty and get the best price", with enough players around the table to create competition.

Beyond Helios, the vision is to build Galaxy's data center business into "a multi-gigawatt, multi-tenant, multi-campus platform": Galaxy has evaluated more than 100 campuses across the US, including many in Texas, and is actively exploring additional markets where power availability, permitting timelines and grid dynamics may offer more attractive paths to accelerate time to power. Novogratz: "we're engaged in conversations with other sites both in Texas and in other states."

FY2025 results (CFO Anthony Paquette): GAAP net loss of $241 million or $0.61 per share, including approximately $160 million of one-time items (among them write-downs and other expenses related to legacy Bitcoin mining infrastructure); $34 million of adjusted EBITDA in 2025. Year-end: $11.3 billion in total assets and over $3 billion in equity capital with roughly 60% allocated to operating businesses (expected to increase over time as digital assets and data centers scale); $2.6 billion of cash and stablecoins. Two Q4 capital raises - a $1.3 billion exchangeable note issuance and a $325 million equity investment by one of the world's largest asset managers (approximately $1.6 billion of net proceeds) - went to continued investment in data center infrastructure and paying down short-term borrowings; future uses focus on the continued data center build and liquidity for potential repayment of the $445 million of exchangeable notes that mature in December 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: GAAP net loss of $241 million ($0.61 per share); $34 million adjusted EBITDA; approximately $1.6 billion net proceeds from Q4 capital raises

connects_to.relationship: Helios campus (West Texas) AI data-center capacity leased to CoreWeave - 800 gross MW across three phases (Phase I 133 MW critical IT delivered; Phase II 260 MW; Phase III 133 MW)

contracts.signal: Ferraro: "800 megawatts now contracted under our lease agreement with CoreWeave"; the first data hall is to be delivered to CoreWeave later in Q1 as part of phase one, with the full 133 megawatts of critical IT for phase one within the first half of the year, and CFO Anthony Paquette expects Galaxy to begin recognizing revenue under Phase one of the CoreWeave lease later in Q1. Novogratz: over a thousand workers are building out the site for CoreWeave, and on CoreWeave "we got paid extra because we took credit risk". Ferraro: Galaxy decided to partner with CoreWeave on the first 800 megawatts, and CoreWeave has emerged "as a one of one partner for most of the large model builders and hyperscalers"; the CoreWeave Helios One side will be fully developed and delivered largely in advance of the next 830 megawatts coming online.
contracts.units: 800 megawatts contracted; 133 megawatts of critical IT (phase one)
contracts.type: AI data-center lease - phase one delivery
